scenes.summary: Edmund examines the victim’s puncture wound and notes the blood pooling on the torn garment, confirming stabbing by a decorative letter opener. He notices the precisely angled mirror at forty-five degrees creating an optical illusion of a continuous corridor, reinforcing the false assumption that the corridor outside the locked room is unbroken. The discrepancy between the theatre clock and street clock times is cross-checked, indicating the time of death was staged.

dramaticElements.conflict: Detective challenges initial assumptions about the crime scene
dramaticElements.tension: Suspects’ stories begin to show cracks
microMomentBeats: Edmund briefly recalls a similar case, deepening his resolve

scenes.title: Dust and Fingerprints
scenes.purpose: Reveal physical evidence linking Percival to hidden access
scenes.summary: Edmund inspects the twelve-inch disturbed dust line along the mirror’s outer edge, indicating recent handling inconsistent with a fixed glass pane. He finds a partial fingerprint smudge matching Percival Orme’s prints, confirming Percival’s contact with the mirror area and suggesting access to a concealed hatch. Percival becomes visibly uneasy as Edmund presses him on this evidence.

dramaticElements.conflict: Percival’s presence near the mirror becomes undeniable
dramaticElements.tension: Percival shows unease under scrutiny
microMomentBeats: Percival’s hands tremble slightly as he denies involvement

scenes.title: The Air Draft
scenes.purpose: Reveal environmental clue confirming hidden hatch
scenes.summary: Edmund detects a faint, unusual air draft near the mirror frame, inconsistent with a sealed wall. Frances tries to dismiss it as a natural ventilation quirk, but Edmund’s observation confirms the presence of a concealed hatch behind the mirror, contradicting the false assumption of an unbroken corridor.

dramaticElements.conflict: Frances attempts to explain away signs of tampering
dramaticElements.tension: Detective grows more certain of secret access
microMomentBeats: Frances glances nervously toward the mirror as Edmund feels the faint draft

scenes.title: The Grease-Stained Weapon
scenes.purpose: Reveal physical evidence linking murder weapon to concealed mechanism
scenes.summary: Edmund finds the decorative letter opener matching the murder weapon with faint grease stains identical to those on the pivot mechanism of the rare-book dealer’s bookshelf. This ties the murder weapon directly to the area adjoining the mirror and suggests premeditation. Percival’s attempts to explain the weapon’s presence are unconvincing.

dramaticElements.conflict: Percival tries to downplay connection to murder weapon
dramaticElements.tension: Detective’s suspicion deepens
microMomentBeats: Percival’s composure cracks briefly when confronted with the grease stains

scenes.title: Ledger Secrets and Alibis
scenes.purpose: Reveal Percival’s ledger entries linking him to mirror maintenance and financial motives
scenes.summary: Edmund studies Percival’s ledger, which notes precise maintenance of the mirror set at forty-five degrees, confirming Percival’s unique knowledge and skill to exploit the optical illusion. The ledger also reveals financial desperation and rivalry with the victim, suggesting premeditation. Percival’s conflicting statements about shop movements raise further suspicion.

dramaticElements.conflict: Percival’s calm facade begins to crack under pressure
dramaticElements.tension: Detective grows confident of Percival’s unique role
microMomentBeats: Percival hesitates before admitting to mirror maintenance details

scenes.title: The Mirror Reflection Test
scenes.purpose: Execute the discriminating test proving the hidden hatch and time staging
scenes.summary: Edmund shines a portable light at the mirror, revealing the optical illusion of continuous space and confirming the hidden hatch’s presence and dimensions—fourteen inches wide. He points out the disturbed dust line and Percival’s fingerprint smudges along the mirror’s edge, confirming secret access. Comparing the theatre clock and street clock times again, Edmund demonstrates the staged time of death, invalidating alibis based on the false assumption. The suspects’ facades begin to crumble.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects react nervously as the illusion is exposed
dramaticElements.tension: Edmund’s test undermines the false assumption and alibis
microMomentBeats: Edmund’s steady voice contrasts with Percival’s tightening jaw

scenes.title: Clearing the Innocent
scenes.purpose: Clear suspects Iris, Oswald, and Frances with solid alibis
scenes.summary: Edmund reviews backstage entry logs and witness testimony confirming Iris Thorne’s presence in the theatre dressing rooms during the crime. Master key logs and security camera maintenance records corroborate Oswald Merrow’s alibi in the theatre control room. Frances Ellery explains the grease stains and presents ledger entries on mirror maintenance, clearing her of direct involvement. The detective narrows suspicion firmly on Percival Orme.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects breathe easier but tensions remain
dramaticElements.tension: Edmund remains focused on the true culprit
microMomentBeats: Iris quietly reflects on her narrow escape from suspicion

scenes.title: The Culprit Revealed
scenes.purpose: Reveal Percival Orme as the murderer and resolve the case
scenes.summary: Edmund confronts Percival Orme with the full array of spatial and physical evidence: the hidden mirror hatch, fingerprint smudges, grease-stained murder weapon, and the staged clock times. A torn page from a rare book bearing Percival’s fingerprint is revealed near the mirror, sealing his guilt. Percival’s carefully maintained facade crumbles, and he confesses his calculated crime motivated by financial desperation and rivalry. The other suspects watch in stunned silence as justice is served.

dramaticElements.conflict: Percival confronted with overwhelming evidence
dramaticElements.tension: Emotional truth surfaces; justice is served
microMomentBeats: Percival’s mask slips, revealing desperation and regret

scenes.title: Discovery
scenes.purpose: Introduce the crime and detective
scenes.summary: Detective Neville Ingram arrives at the English Coastal Hotel to find Adela Ashgrove dead in the manager’s office, her head bruised and bloodied near a heavy brass paperweight. The suspects are gathered, each with potential access to the victim. Neville notices blotchy ink patches on the chemical order ledger dated the day of the murder, raising his first doubts about the reliability of the record.

dramaticElements.conflict: Locked room mystery established with a puzzling time discrepancy
dramaticElements.tension: Every suspect had access to the victim and the ledger
microMomentBeats: Dorothy Carrick pauses at the doorway, her grief barely concealed

scenes.title: Conflicting Times
scenes.purpose: Establish key contradiction between clocks and records
scenes.summary: Neville compares the hotel tide clock showing high tide at quarter past four with the independent tide table indicating high tide at five minutes past four, revealing a ten-minute discrepancy. This contradiction casts doubt on the ledger’s timestamps, which rely on the hotel’s internal timing. The suspects exchange glances, unease growing as the detective probes the timeline.

dramaticElements.conflict: Two clocks show contradictory times, undermining the ledger’s timeline
dramaticElements.tension: Suspects grow uneasy as the detective questions the timeline
microMomentBeats: Neville briefly recalls his war experiences, feeling the weight of responsibility

scenes.title: Ink and Bruises
scenes.purpose: Reveal physical and forensic clues undermining ledger authenticity
scenes.summary: Neville examines the ledger closely, noting the handwriting pressure on the forged entry differs with lighter strokes and inconsistent ink flow. Chemical solvent use is evident from blotchy ink patches. Nearby, the victim’s fresh head bruise and bloodied heavy brass paperweight confirm a violent struggle. Lavinia Yardley watches silently, her composure hinting at concealed knowledge.

dramaticElements.conflict: Physical evidence contradicts ledger’s timeline and casts suspicion on ledger manipulation
dramaticElements.tension: Lavinia’s calm demeanor contrasts with the incriminating ink evidence
microMomentBeats: Lavinia briefly falters when questioned about the ledger, betraying inner conflict

scenes.title: Diary Secrets
scenes.purpose: Reveal diary note that contradicts ledger timestamp and begin narrowing suspects
scenes.summary: Neville studies the chemist’s private diary and discovers a note stating the actual chemical delivery arrived after seven fifteen, contradicting the ledger’s forged timestamp of half past six. This revelation indicates deliberate falsification to shift the timeline. Dorothy Carrick and Katherine Jardine appear unsettled by this, raising suspicion about the ledger’s authenticity.

dramaticElements.conflict: Diary note contradicts ledger timestamp, casting doubt on forged entry
dramaticElements.tension: Dorothy and Katherine exchange uneasy glances as ledger’s reliability is questioned
microMomentBeats: Neville reflects on the weight of trust placed on official records

scenes.title: Alibis Under Scrutiny
scenes.purpose: Test alibis and reveal contradictions with timeline
scenes.summary: Neville interrogates Lavinia Yardley about her alibi covering four o’clock to six thirty in the manager’s office, but physical evidence and the corrected timeline place the victim’s death at quarter past three. This contradiction implies Lavinia’s alibi is incomplete or false. Dorothy and Katherine observe the exchange, their own alibis under silent scrutiny.

dramaticElements.conflict: Lavinia’s alibi fails to cover actual time of death, increasing suspicion
dramaticElements.tension: Lavinia grows defensive while others watch closely
microMomentBeats: Neville senses Lavinia’s unease and questions his own judgment

scenes.title: Illicit Concealments
scenes.purpose: Reveal Lavinia’s secretive behaviour and suspicious access
scenes.summary: Neville uncovers evidence that Lavinia Yardley was observed concealing illicit chemical usage in management files, presumably to protect the hotel’s reputation. Her fingerprints are found on the ledger, confirming her access and opportunity to manipulate entries. Ferdinand Underhill’s guarded presence adds to the charged atmosphere as loyalties and secrets simmer.

dramaticElements.conflict: Lavinia’s concealment of illicit chemical usage raises suspicion
dramaticElements.tension: Ferdinand watches Lavinia warily, hinting at unspoken knowledge
microMomentBeats: Neville feels the weight of betrayal as trust erodes

scenes.title: Unearthing the Pattern
scenes.purpose: Reconstruct timeline and prepare for final test
scenes.summary: Neville oversees a forensic examination comparing the ledger’s ink patches and handwriting pressure with samples from the manager’s known writing implements. The test confirms forgery and chemical solvent use in ink alteration. Lavinia Yardley’s unique handwriting traits and access patterns emerge, invalidating her alibi and exposing the false timeline. The pieces align, setting the stage for a trap.

dramaticElements.conflict: Forensic examination exposes ledger forgery and handwriting inconsistencies
dramaticElements.tension: Lavinia’s composure cracks slightly under scrutiny
microMomentBeats: Neville steels himself for the decisive confrontation

scenes.title: The Discriminating Test
scenes.purpose: Execute the forensic trap to expose the forgery and culprit
scenes.summary: Neville stages a forensic trap by demonstrating the ink patch alterations and handwriting pressure discrepancies on the ledger, using manager’s known writing samples and implements. Lavinia Yardley’s reaction—visible discomfort and evasiveness—betrays her guilt. The test conclusively proves the ledger entry was forged to falsify the timeline and conceal the murder time.

dramaticElements.conflict: Lavinia’s reaction betrays guilt as the test confirms forgery
dramaticElements.tension: Silent room as Neville reveals the test results
microMomentBeats: Lavinia’s composure falters, revealing inner turmoil

scenes.title: Clearing the Innocents
scenes.purpose: Clear suspects and victim by alibi and timeline analysis
scenes.summary: Neville methodically clears Dorothy Carrick by confirming her alibi in the laboratory and the physical ink evidence excluding her involvement. Katherine Jardine is eliminated due to handwriting pressure inconsistencies and her alibi in the hotel dining room. Ferdinand Underhill’s presence in the private office and lack of ledger access also excludes him. The victim, Adela Ashgrove, is reaffirmed as deceased prior to the key timeline, confirming no posthumous involvement.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects wrestle with relief and lingering doubts
dramaticElements.tension: Uneasy peace as suspicions are laid to rest
microMomentBeats: Dorothy’s subtle sigh of relief; Ferdinand’s quiet nod of acceptance

scenes.title: The Culprit Unmasked
scenes.purpose: Confront Lavinia with the full evidence and reveal the truth
scenes.summary: Neville confronts Lavinia Yardley with the forensic evidence of ledger forgery and the corrected timeline proving the victim died before her claimed alibi period. Lavinia’s carefully constructed false timeline is exposed as a deliberate attempt to conceal her opportunity to commit the poisoning. Facing the evidence, Lavinia’s composure breaks, revealing her motive and guilt.

dramaticElements.conflict: Lavinia confronted with irrefutable evidence and timeline contradiction
dramaticElements.tension: Emotional climax as Lavinia’s defenses crumble
microMomentBeats: Lavinia’s moment of silence before her confession or breakdown

scenes.title: Discovery
scenes.purpose: Introduce the crime and detective
scenes.summary: Montague Penhale arrives at the village hall foyer and immediately discovers the body of Dr. Edith Ormesby. As he surveys the scene, he notes the presence of the other suspects and witnesses gathered. His attention is drawn to a faint brushstroke pattern on the wall behind the oil lamp, suggesting the shadow there may not be what it seems.

dramaticElements.conflict: Locked room mystery established
dramaticElements.tension: Every suspect had access to the victim
microMomentBeats: Montague hesitates before entering the foyer, feeling unease at the painted shadow

scenes.title: Flickering Shadows
scenes.purpose: Establish the unnatural nature of the shadow and deepen mystery
scenes.summary: Montague closely observes the oil lamp flickering at twenty flickers per minute and notices the shadow on the wall remains perfectly still without any distortion expected from a living silhouette. Quentin and Leonard watch uneasily as Montague voices his doubts about the witness accounts.

dramaticElements.conflict: Montague questions the reliability of eyewitnesses
dramaticElements.tension: The shadow remains perfectly still despite the flickering lamp
microMomentBeats: Montague pauses, unsettled by the unnatural stillness of the shadow

scenes.title: Likeness and Wounds
scenes.purpose: Reveal early mechanism detail and victim’s wound; introduce contradiction
scenes.summary: Montague inspects the painted silhouette of Dr. Edith Ormesby on the wall, noting it is positioned fourteen feet from the oil lamp and matches the shadow’s height of six feet two inches. He also examines the victim's puncture wound consistent with stabbing by a decorative letter opener. The static nature of the shadow contradicts witness assumptions, deepening the mystery.

dramaticElements.conflict: Montague confronts the impossibility of the shadow being Edith
dramaticElements.tension: Quentin appears uneasy when Montague points to the painted silhouette
microMomentBeats: Quentin briefly touches his bandaged hand, betraying hidden anxiety

scenes.title: Conflicting Witnesses
scenes.purpose: Reveal contradictions in witness testimonies and begin suspect elimination
scenes.summary: Montague interviews Hector, Ivor, and Leonard, who each recount their version of events. He reveals that no footprints or dust disturbances were found near the painted shadow despite multiple witnesses claiming Edith stood there. This absence of physical traces contradicts their testimonies and begins to unravel the false assumption.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects argue over whereabouts and witness reliability
dramaticElements.tension: Montague senses tension rising as alibis begin to fray
microMomentBeats: Hector glances nervously at the doorway as accusations fly

scenes.title: Quentin's Coat and Bandage
scenes.purpose: Reveal Quentin’s impersonation and physical evidence linking him to the painted shadow
scenes.summary: Montague confronts Quentin about his distinctive dark wool coat and a faint bandage on his hand, which match witness reports of a figure impersonating Edith in the foyer. Quentin’s evasive answers hint at premeditation and a desire to overshadow Edith, deepening suspicion.

dramaticElements.conflict: Montague presses Quentin on his suspicious attire and actions
dramaticElements.tension: Quentin grows defensive but tries to maintain composure
microMomentBeats: Quentin nervously adjusts the bandage on his hand

scenes.title: Eliminations Begin
scenes.purpose: Narrow suspects by verifying alibis and eliminating innocent parties
scenes.summary: Montague carefully cross-checks alibis, confirming Hector was at the forge, Ivor in the meeting room, and Leonard on the village green at the time of the murder. Montague’s own alibi is corroborated, narrowing suspicion toward Quentin Everleigh who lacks a full alibi.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects react to being cleared; some frustration and relief
dramaticElements.tension: Montague grows more isolated in his suspicions
microMomentBeats: Ivor sighs with relief, while Hector looks away, unsettled

scenes.title: Secrets and Lies
scenes.purpose: Uncover unrelated lies and explain earlier red herrings
scenes.summary: Montague uncovers personal deceptions among Hector, Ivor, and Leonard that clarify earlier misleading testimony, including the false belief that Edith was physically present in the foyer. The shadow is confirmed as a painted silhouette, disproving Edith’s presence at ten twenty past nine.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects reveal personal secrets unrelated to the murder
dramaticElements.tension: Montague feels the weight of moral guilt vs criminal guilt
microMomentBeats: Leonard looks remorseful as he admits to protecting Hector

scenes.title: Discriminating Test
scenes.purpose: Execute the discriminating test to prove the shadow is painted and expose the spatial illusion
scenes.summary: Montague stages a controlled observation by lighting the oil lamp at twenty flickers per minute and directing all eyes to the painted wall. The shadow remains perfectly still, and close inspection reveals brushstroke patterns. This constraint proof definitively shows the shadow is artificial, disproving all eyewitness accounts placing Edith in the foyer at the critical time and exposing the true murder location.

dramaticElements.conflict: Quentin tries to deflect but cannot explain the test results
dramaticElements.tension: The room holds its breath as the lamp flickers and the shadow remains still
microMomentBeats: Montague’s steady gaze unsettles Quentin, who shifts nervously

scenes.title: Clearing the Innocent
scenes.purpose: Confirm alibis and clear suspects including the victim’s confirmed location
scenes.summary: Montague verifies Hector’s alibi at the forge, confirmed by the condition of the forge hammer and apprentice testimony. Ivor’s presence in the meeting room is supported by witness accounts and meeting records. Leonard’s alibi on the village green is upheld by footprint analysis and witness statements. Dr. Edith Ormesby’s confirmed alibi from nine zero to nine ten alone in the adjoining poets' circle room is established, solidifying the timeline and excluding them from the foyer at the critical time.

dramaticElements.conflict: Suspects show mixed relief and residual guilt
dramaticElements.tension: Montague’s calm but firm tone underscores the gravity of the revelations
microMomentBeats: Hector exhales deeply, accepting his moral burden
Ivor looks distant, wrestling with regret
Leonard’s eyes betray conflicted loyalty

scenes.title: Confronting Quentin Everleigh
scenes.purpose: Reveal Quentin Everleigh as culprit using spatial illusion and impersonation evidence
scenes.summary: Montague confronts Quentin with the results of the discriminating test and the evidence of his dark wool coat and hand bandage matching the impostor seen impersonating Edith. The spatial illusion is exposed as a deliberate deception orchestrated by Quentin to conceal the true murder location. Quentin’s motives and actions come to light, culminating in his exposure as the murderer.

dramaticElements.conflict: Quentin faces undeniable proof and mounting pressure
dramaticElements.tension: The confrontation escalates to a breaking point
microMomentBeats: Quentin’s composure cracks as Montague lays out the evidence
